newsitem.title: FRANCE: Findings of draft European BSE inquiry report.
newsitem.headline: Findings of draft European BSE inquiry report.

text.p: A draft European Parliament committee of inquiry report strongly attacks Britain and the European Commission for mishandling the mad cow crisis, but it is unclear at present whether sanctions will be proposed.
Below are the key findings of the report, drafted by Spanish Socialist Euro-MP Manuel Medina Ortega. It is still open to change before it is finalised on February 6.
It will be put to the full Parliament for adoption on February 19. Britain and the Commission contest the findings.

* The report criticises the European Commission for delaying the release of data on Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), saying this helped to undermine public confidence and worsen the economic damage.
It says the division of responsibilities in the Commission was unclear.
* The report attacks the British government's handling of the crisis, identifying 13 points of alleged negligence.
- It says London failed properly to enforce a ban on exports of animal feed for ruminants which contained meat and bone meal.
- London also failed to respect national legislation outlawing imports by other EU countries of meat and bone meal from Britain.
- Britain pressured the European Commission to avoid inspecting British slaughterhouses between 1990-94.
- It tightened this pressure by increasing the presence of its officials and scientific experts on EU bodies.
- It did not take scientific evidence and advice seriously.
- It did not honour a promise to EU partners to introduce checks on herds in which BSE had been detected.
- It did not implement legislation under which bovines should have been identified and branded and their movements registered.
- It failed to implement EU rules on veterinary checks by failing to carry out checks on all animal products leaving its territory for the EU market.
- It adopted a blocking policy in the EU in a bid to force the EU to lift an embargo on British beef.
- It did not respect the embargo.
- It did not honour an agreement struck with its EU partners at the Florence Summit on a selected culling programme, which was suspended with no alternative proposal put forward.
- British Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg is accused of refusing to appear before the Parliament's Committee of Inquiry.
- The report says the British government, through its attitude, failed to ensure the proper application of legislation and did not carry out necessary checks.

* The report says there should be an independent agency to protect public and animal welfare. It says that would help reinforce controls to ensure that export bans and other measures to combat mad cow disease were properly implemented.
